verdict: Avoid new export-led readymade garment exposure in Noida; lend only to domestic-focused, funded-order borrowers with tight structure.
title: Noida Readymade Garments & Made-ups: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
A Noida garment unit cuts, stitches and finishes fabric into export or domestic apparel, converting cloth into cash only when a buyer lifts and pays. **Cash sits in fabric inventory and in receivables, not in the sewing floor.** Fabric is the largest cost line and inventory holding plus receivables drive working capital [8]. So when a proposal lands, check the order book and buyer names first; if the buyer list is one or two US accounts, ask for the last six months of order confirmations.

## What has broken now
Noida's operational apparel units fell from 2,400 to 1,800 in six months as orders dried up [2], and exporters are cutting output and delaying reopening on US demand weakness and tariff uncertainty [1]. **This is a demand-and-planning shock, not a cost shock.** Nationally, IIP for NIC 14 is -7.4% YoY and -5.6% Apr-to-date [D], and exports are -6.2% Apr-to-date in USD [D]. Bank credit to the sector is +23.3% YoY against that output fall [D], so the system is lending into a shrinking order book. Treat that gap as a warning on peer underwriting, not as comfort.

## Where growth actually is
Domestic demand is the growth engine; export-dependent books will moderate [10]. Peer results split the same way: Raymond's garmenting order book runs to mid-Feb'27 with rising European traction [4], while Kewal Kiran's growth leans on festive domestic volume with discretionary softness flagged [6]. **Pursue domestic-brand and made-ups suppliers with confirmed purchase orders, and job-work units tied to a funded buyer.** Avoid pure US-export converters, units with idle shifts, and any borrower whose sanction rests on orders not yet confirmed. Note the sources say little on Noida-specific domestic order flow, so lean on first principles and these peers.

## How to grow safely
Structure against the order, not the balance sheet. **Fund a percentage of confirmed receivables, keep inventory out of the drawing power, and take the buyer's payment routing where possible.** Take monthly stock-and-receivable statements, monthly order-book position, and quarterly buyer-wise sales concentration. Ask for the export realisation statement each month where any export exposure remains. The Ministry's TEXPORT capacity programme in Noida through AEPC [3] is a useful signal that compliant, scheme-linked units exist; prefer those.

## Early-warning signs
- Unit operating below full shifts or reopening delayed after a shutdown [1][2] -> freeze fresh limits and re-assess the order book.
- Buyer concentration above two accounts with no confirmed forward orders -> ask for order confirmations and shift to receivable-only funding.
- Receivable days stretching month on month -> ask for buyer-wise ageing and stop inventory funding.
- Any proposal resting on unconfirmed US orders -> decline or restructure to confirmed-order backing only.
